title: Nimbus day-ahead battery plan
subtitle: The next 24 hours as the solver published them at 11:56 AEST on Thu 4 Sep: what the 100 kWh battery charges, when it carries the house, and where the plan's confidence is thinnest.
stamp_extra: Amber (QLD1) · Solcast · 5-min periods · export sensor: Amber feed-in

callouts.text: Grid charge at 2.7–4.9 ¢. 74 kWh bought 11:56–16:00 with import pinned at the 30 kW cap and charging at the 21 kW cap; solar covers the rest of the 23 kW midday load.
Full at 15:55, five minutes before the cliff. Import price steps from 4.3 ¢ to 30.1 ¢ at 16:00.
15 h discharge, 92.6 kWh. Battery matches the 6 kW evening load; zero grid import 16:00–22:00 through the 32.5 ¢ peak at 17:30.
Overnight low, 15.0 ¢. 5.2 kWh imported at 02:00 and discharge eased to 1.8 kW, keeping stored energy for the 17.5 ¢ hours at 05:00–06:00.
Empty at 06:55, floor for 2.6 h. The 07:00–09:00 shoulder (10.6–11.6 ¢) is served from the grid: 5.8 kWh. No reserve survives the night.
Forecast fallback from 03:35. 101 of 292 periods use the pd7day blend rather than raw Amber. Tomorrow’s 09:30 recharge (24.5 kWh at 3–10 ¢) is decided on it.
Export worth nothing. Feed-in peaks at 7.4 ¢ and is −2.3 ¢ midday, so 0 kWh exported and solar goes to load and battery instead.

strengths: Clean two-block arbitrage. 74 kWh bought at 2.7–4.9 ¢ between 11:56 and 16:00, then 92.6 kWh returned to the house at 15–32 ¢ from 16:00 to 07:00. Effective grid cost for the day is $6.24 for 240.6 kWh of load, about 2.6 ¢/kWh.
Timing to the cliff. Full (100 %) at 15:55; the import price steps from 4.3 ¢ to 30.1 ¢ at 16:00. No headroom is wasted and nothing is bought at peak.
Peak covered entirely. Zero grid import from 16:00 to 22:00 (32.5 ¢ peak at 17:30). Battery discharge tracks the 6 kW evening load one-to-one instead of dumping.
Export correctly suppressed. Feed-in never exceeds 7.4 ¢ and is negative midday (−2.3 ¢), so 0 kWh exported and no simultaneous import/export in any period.
Both hardware limits used. 35 periods pinned at the 30 kW import cap and 24 at the 21 kW charge cap, with solar covering the gap to the 23 kW midday load.
Intelligent overnight shaving. At 02:00, the overnight price low (15.0 ¢), it imports 5.2 kWh and eases discharge so stored energy is kept for the 17.5 ¢ hours at 05:00–06:00.
weaknesses: Empty for the morning shoulder. SoC hits the 5 % floor at 06:55 and stays there 2.6 h while 07:00–09:00 prices sit at 10.6–11.6 ¢ (5.8 kWh imported). No reserve is left for a morning spike; risk aversion is only 0.05.

Load forecast disagrees with the meter now. The ML load input reads 22.3 kW while the whole-house meter reads 16.5 kW, a 35 % gap, and the coordinator has logged residual drift at 4× its baseline today. Midday load of 21–23 kW drives the 30 kW import pin; if it is high, the plan over-buys.

Degradation is the second-largest cost. 0.03 $/kWh on 191 kWh of throughput is ≈$5.74 for the day, nearly equal to the grid bill, and $22.1 of the $62 four-day total. If the real per-cycle cost is lower the plan is too shy; if higher it is over-cycling (3.7 full cycles in 96 h).

Tomorrow rests on a forecast blend. From 03:35 the blended price departs from the raw Amber feed (101 of 292 periods use the pd7day fallback). Tomorrow's 09:30 recharge, 24.5 kWh at 3–10 ¢, is decided on that blend, not on Amber's own forecast.
Wide uncertainty band. The 96 h expected cost is $62 with a band of $19 to $80. With export worthless the plan is fully exposed to midday import price, and a spike there has no hedge.
Missing temperature feature. weather.home returns no hourly forecast, so the load model trains without temperature, which matters for a house whose evening load is dominated by climate.

yesterday.subtitle: Nimbus's own quality report scores the day the battery actually had (driven by HAEO, with Nimbus in shadow) against a perfect-foresight oracle and an idle-battery reference. EPR 35.5 %: idle $5.56 → achieved $0.97 → oracle −$7.37, regret $8.34.

callouts.text: $8.40 of regret in four hours. Achieved held ~31 % from 20:00; the oracle exported up to 22 kW at 12–13 ¢ and ran to 5.5 %.
Oracle exports 11 kW at 6.8 ¢ at midnight. Only "optimal" because the scoring LP carries no degradation cost; net of the household’s 5 ¢ of fees + degradation it is worth nothing.
Real SoC hit 1.0 % at 08:00 (below the 5 % floor) while the scored trajectory says 29 %. Battery power read idle overnight as SoC fell 26 points.
Real 81 % vs scored 70 % at 14:00. A 32-point charge the battery-power sensor did not record (−0.4 kW mean). The scored day closes at 31 %; the real one at 27 %.
Dawn export at 6.4 ¢ books $0.52 of regret for the same degradation-free reason as callout 2.

lessons: The regret is one decision. $8.4 of the $8.34 total sits in 19:00–22:00. The achieved dispatch stopped discharging near 31 % and carried ~26 kWh through 12–13 ¢ export and 37–39 ¢ import, while the oracle ran the pack to 5.5 % exporting up to 22 kW. Nimbus's own counterfactual says it would have closed at 19.2 % rather than the real 25.5 %: in the oracle's direction, but still holding a reserve.

The oracle cycles free. The report's oracle and reference LPs are built without degradation_cost_per_kwh (it defaults to 0; the live plan pays 3 ¢/kWh). Re-priced at 3 ¢, the oracle's 217 kWh of throughput costs ~$6.5 and the achieved 87 kWh ~$2.6; the defensible missed value is closer to $3 than $8.

"Achieved" is a model, not a measurement. The scored trajectory is integrated from sensor.sigen_plant_battery_power, but the configured SoC sensor is sensor.combined_soc. The recorder shows SoC falling 31.8 → 6.2 % overnight and touching 1.0 % at 08:00 while battery power reads idle, and a +32 % jump at 14:00 while power reads −0.4 kW. The scored day closes at 31.4 %; the real one at 26.6 %.
Tracking fidelity is vacuous in shadow mode. 1.0 / $0.00 says nothing while Nimbus issues no commands.

Today's plan over-corrects the same risk. Yesterday's real system reached 1 % at 08:00; today's plan deliberately sits on the 5 % floor from 06:55. The reserve question is the parameter both days turn on.

footnote: Source: Home Assistant diagnostics dump for the Nimbus config entry, downloaded 12:00 AEST 4 Sep 2026 (sensor.nimbus_solver_battery_forecast, 364-period horizon, first 292 periods shown); yesterday's scoring from sensor.nimbus_solver_quality_report (cross-checked with the compute_quality_report service for the same window, identical) and hourly recorder statistics for the real SoC and prices. Prices are ¢/kWh after Nimbus's primary-preferring blend of the retailer feed with the forecast fallback; power is AC-side kW; battery sign is positive-discharge. The fixed daily supply charge is excluded from the day cost shown.
